final.title: When AI answers go off track, narrow the workflow
final.body:
If you run a one-person business, the issue with ChatGPT is not that it sounds confident. It is that it can drift outside the process you already trust. That is a control problem.

The practical question is simple: can this task be bounded by your own documents, past answers, rules, or procedures? If yes, then AI can be kept inside approved company material before it answers. In plain terms, it looks in your material rather than the open web. That constrains invented answers; it does not make risk disappear.

So ask yourself this: “Do I have a pile of answers, documents, or procedures I already trust, and am I asking the AI to answer only from that pile?” If the answer is yes, the next step is a small pilot inside your own environment, using your own data and tools, with code and accounts kept in your name. Treat the timing as scope, not a promise.

If the answer is no, or you are still unsure, keep the work manual for now or hire for it. That is often the cleaner choice than asking a model to improvise where precision matters. AI is helpful, but it is not a replacement for judgment. Not on a Tuesday afternoon, anyway.

final.title: When AI hallucinates, narrow the workflow
final.body:
If you run a one-person business, the issue is not that AI sometimes sounds confident. The issue is that it can answer outside the process you wanted it to follow. That is a control problem, not a personality problem.

So make one decision first: can this workflow be bounded by material you already trust? By that I mean your own documents, past answers, rules, or procedures. If the answer is yes, the AI should retrieve from approved company material before it answers. In plain English, that is a grounded workflow: it looks in your material instead of the open web. That does not remove hallucination risk, but it does narrow it.

Use one diagnostic question: “Do I have a pile of answers, documents, or procedures I already trust, and am I asking the AI to answer only from that pile?” If yes, start with a small pilot inside your own environment, using your own data and tools, with code and accounts in your name. Treat the timing as an intended scope, not a promise.

If the answer is no, or you are still unsure, keep the task manual for now or hire for it. Sometimes the honest workflow is the boring one, which is usually a good sign.
